LESSON: WRITING 2.3.1 ESSAY WRITING

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Writing 2.3.1 Essay writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.3.1 Essay writing, part of Strand 2 in Grade 7 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we write an essay?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read in class, sample essays and identify the three parts,

2. identify ideas from sample essays,

3. read essays aloud in class and correct mistakes,

4. select a topic, write a simple essay, and share with other learners,

5. search for more information about essay writing from the library or digital sources,

6. display essays in the class creative corner.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read in class, sample essays and identify the three parts,
2. identify ideas from sample essays,
3. read essays aloud in class and correct mistakes,
4. select a topic, write a simple essay, and share with other learners,
5. search for more information about essay writing from the library or digital sources,
6. display essays in the class creative corner.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.3.1 Essay writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: This is developed as the learner searches for information on essay writing from digital sources.

• Communication and collaboration: Communication skills are developed as the learner writes essays on selected topics.

Values:
• Responsibility: This is exercised as the learner identifies an idea and selects a topic for essay writing.

• Respect: This is observed as the learner reads sample essays with other learners in class.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social Cohesion is enhanced as the learner participates in reading and identifying ideas from sample essays in class.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can apply the skill of essay writing to other subjects like English and Kiswahili languages.
